transcript: Last night, I saw the first 3/4 of the opening night performance of Between Two Knees at PAC NYC, before the rest of the performance was unfortunately cancelled due to an actor injury — but more on that later. This was my first time attending a show at this venue and it's very beautiful, very shiny and new. In the lobby, we had some pre-show remarks and then a performance from the Lenape Center, which was quite apt given the subject matter of the play. Between Two Knees is a comedic romp through Native American history beginning with the 1890 massacre at Wounded Knee. We focus on one family through multiple decades as they face genocide, war and forced relocation, among other things. Despite the subject matter, this play is funny. The type of comedy isn't for everyone, it's ridiculous, very crude, physical, and pointed. Actually, the audience is directly addressed throughout the piece and you're very much confronted with this dark aspect of American history. The stylistic campiness, however, cuts the tension and keeps the show buoyant and entertaining while remaining educational. I had a good time and it definitely helped being with an enthusiastic opening night audience. Now, I can't give a full review because like I mentioned, I didn't see the full play. Unfortunately, the performance was cancelled part way through Act 2 because a performer sustained an injury backstage. For this to happen on opening night is possibly the worst luck ever, but hey, anything can happen with live theater. We at least got some closing remarks from the director and some of the folks who wrote the piece and then the actors came out for a makeshift curtain call. It was definitely a bummer, but the audience was nothing but supportive and we were already really satisfied with our experience up to that point, and we still had the opening night reception. Overall, it was a very eventful evening. If this piece seems up your alley, Between Two Knees is running through February 24th at the Perelman Performing Arts Center in the Financial District. With that, another program for my collection.
